introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

figures.legende: Part (i): three forces on a particle P: T pointing up and to the left, F horizontal to the right, 200 N vertically downwards; the angle of 120 degrees is marked between T and the 200 N force and a right angle between F and the 200 N force.

incertitudes: Q11(i) : le dessin est fait a main levee et n'est pas a l'echelle (T y semble faire environ 60 degres avec l'horizontale). Lecture retenue : l'arc de 120 degres est entre T et la force de 200 N (T a 30 degres au-dessus de l'horizontale), d'ou T = 400 N et F = 200 racine de 3 = 346,4 N (valeurs rondes). Si 120 degres etait l'angle entre T et F, on aurait T = 230,9 N et F = 115,5 N.

Q11(ii)(b) : le sujet dit « the acceleration of the car on a horizontal » ; lu comme une route horizontale, meme puissance (60 kW) et meme resistance (2000 N) : a = 10 m/s^2. Si la voiture etait encore sur la pente, a = (12000 - 2000 - 1000)/1000 = 9 m/s^2. Le texte imprime contient aussi une coquille (« the speed of the is 5 ms^-1 »), lue comme la vitesse de la voiture.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) The diagram above shows three forces $T$, $F$ and $200$ N acting on a particle $P$, which is in equilibrium. Find the magnitude of $T$ and $F$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the diagram.** The $200$ N force acts vertically downwards, $F$ acts horizontally to the right (the small square marks a right angle between $F$ and the $200$ N force) and $T$ acts up and to the left. The angle marked $120^\circ$ is the angle between $T$ and the $200$ N force (the arc goes from $T$ round to the downward vertical). So $T$ makes $120^\circ$ with the downward vertical, which is $30^\circ$ above the horizontal (on the left).

**Equilibrium:** the sum of the components in each direction is zero.

Vertically (up positive): $T\sin30^\circ-200=0\ \Rightarrow\ T\times\dfrac12=200\ \Rightarrow\ T=400.$

Horizontally (right positive): $F-T\cos30^\circ=0\ \Rightarrow\ F=400\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=200\sqrt3\approx346.4.$

**Check with Lami's theorem** (each force over the sine of the angle between the other two): the angles are $T,F$: $150^\circ$; $F,200$: $90^\circ$; $T,200$: $120^\circ$, so

$$\frac{T}{\sin90^\circ}=\frac{F}{\sin120^\circ}=\frac{200}{\sin150^\circ}=400,$$

which gives $T=400$ and $F=400\sin120^\circ=346.4$ ✓.

**$T=400$ N and $F=200\sqrt3\approx346.4$ N.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A car of mass $1000$ kg, moving up a plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta=\dfrac1{10}$, generates a constant power of $60$ kW against a constant resistance to motion of $2000$ N. Find

(a) the maximum speed of the car up the plane. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F$ balances the resistance and the component of the weight down the slope:

$$F=2000+mg\sin\theta=2000+1000\times10\times\frac1{10}=2000+1000=3000\ \text{N}.$$

Power $=$ driving force $\times$ speed, with $P=60\,000$ W:

$$v=\frac{P}{F}=\frac{60\,000}{3000}=20.$$

**The maximum speed of the car up the plane is $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) the acceleration of the car on a horizontal [road] at the instant when the speed of the car is $5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
On a horizontal road there is no weight component along the motion, so the only resisting force is the $2000$ N resistance. The car still generates $60\,000$ W.

Driving force at $v=5$: $F=\dfrac{P}{v}=\dfrac{60\,000}{5}=12\,000$ N.

Newton's second law: $F-R=ma$:

$$12\,000-2000=1000a\ \Rightarrow\ a=\frac{10\,000}{1000}=10.$$

**The acceleration is $10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle
